bridges.statement: Mental properties cannot be identical with or reduced to physical brain properties.
A soul best grounds unified consciousness, indivisible personhood, and identity through change.
Libertarian agency requires a nonphysical personal originator.
Brain dependence is compatible with a soul using the brain as an instrument.
Metaphysical reasoning can establish truths that empirical science alone cannot establish.

routes.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
routes.position: No soul has been shown to exist

bridges.statement: No soul has been reliably demonstrated.
Split-brain and brain-damage observations support dependence of attributed soul functions on brains.
A proposed soul explanation needs a reliable method and evidence of necessity, not mere compatibility.
Physical and emergent accounts remain viable alternatives to a soul.
Any soul that affects material reality should produce detectable manifestations.
Continuing identity can be understood through practical labels applied to changing physical persons.
Agency and rational belief do not require libertarian freedom.

sections.title: Mental Properties, Explanation, and Testability
sections.rationale: The exchange contrasts property-dualist arguments about mentality with demands that soul explanations be necessary, noncircular, and empirically contactable.

sections.title: Unity, Personhood, and Brain Dependence
sections.rationale: Unified experience, indivisibility, and enduring identity meet split-brain, injury, practical-label, and retrieval-instrument accounts of personal continuity.

sections.title: Emergence, Neuroplasticity, and Physicalism
sections.rationale: The speakers compare neuroplastic top-down causation and physicalism's alleged costs with emergence, epistemic restraint, and a reliable-method requirement.

sections.title: Free Will, Determinism, and Rationality
sections.rationale: Libertarian alternative ability and proposed demonstrations of freedom meet compatibilist agency, programmed-response counterexamples, causal explanation, and truth-independent belief formation.

sections.title: Mind, Identity, and Entity Verification
sections.rationale: The later cross-examination tests qualia, latent capacities, and the seven-argument burden against brain production, divided subjects, package individuation, and entity-demonstration objections.

sections.title: Interaction, Brain Injury, and Survival Evidence
sections.rationale: Audience questions connect the soul-of-the-gaps dispute, causal interaction, injury, near-death evidence, and epistemic trust to the motion.

sections.title: Closing Burdens and Summations
sections.rationale: The final exchange directly contrasts an allegedly undefeated seven-argument case with the claim that no soul entity or physical impossibility was demonstrated.
